task_instance: Convert a minimal two-photon imaging session to a validated NWB file: a small multi-page grayscale TIFF stack plus a frame-timestamp CSV and a calibrated position CSV (time_s,x,y in cm), run through the skill's bundled scripts/convert_session.py with a filled-in session-template.json, producing session.nwb and its session.validation.json (schema check, NWB Inspector findings, round-trip equality).
blocker_detail: The skill's only stated path to its deliverable is executing the bundled Python converter (scripts/convert_session.py) inside a pinned Python 3.12 environment built with a package installer (NeuroConv, PyNWB, NWB Inspector, roiextractors, tifffile, zarr, hdmf-zarr). The office-assistant runtime cannot run code or shell commands, cannot install software, and cannot read/write binary files. The core inputs (a multi-page TIFF image stack) and the core deliverable (an NWB file, which is a binary HDF5 container) are binary and cannot be produced or verified here, and the converter cannot be executed. Per the run rules I did not write my own replacement/stub for the missing-execution script. The skill's own files (SKILL.md, scripts/convert_session.py, assets/session-template.json, references/) are all present, so this is not a missing-skill-file case; it is purely the absence of code execution and binary-file abilities in this runtime.
evidence: Read the SKILL.md: its 'Install the tested environment', 'Execute' and 'Workflow' sections mandate (a) building a Python 3.12 virtual environment and installing seven pinned packages via a package manager, and (b) running 'nwb-env/bin/python scripts/convert_session.py <session.json> --output <session.nwb>' to emit the NWB (HDF5 binary) file plus a .validation.json. Confirmed the bundled files exist next to SKILL.md: scripts/convert_session.py (16098 bytes) and assets/session-template.json (1340 bytes), plus a references/ directory, so no skill file is missing. The office-assistant runtime grants only text file read/write/edit and (disabled for this run) web access; it explicitly cannot run any code, install packages, or produce binary files. A representative TIFF image input is itself a binary file that cannot be created here, and the NWB output is binary HDF5. No text-only substitute produces or verifies the real deliverable, so the attempt stops at the first required step (environment install / script execution). No deliverable file was produced.
